header: Date: 2026-03-05 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Tom (Ironclad Head of ML), Aisha (VP Eng), Leo (Infra), Nina (PM)
summary: Ironclad is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for LLM inference. Primary focus: unit economics (per-token cost), batching and caching levers, budget constraint (~$15k-$25k/mo target), SLAs and security (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Redwood AE/SE walked through high-level cost model, expected savings on Dedicated with commits, and pilot next steps (benchmark run). Customer to share traffic profile; Redwood to send cost spreadsheet and security docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros then we'll dive into cost / econ, that was the ask on the invite.
[00:12] Tom (Ironclad): Hey Samir, Tom here, head of ML. Aisha and Leo are with me, thanks.
[00:18] Jenna (Redwood SE): Hi all, Jenna, I'll be the SE on the pilot. Quick note, some product names might come out a bit off in the transcript, sorry in advance.
[00:25] Aisha (Ironclad): No worries.
[00:30] Samir: Great. So to frame, Ironclad said budget target around 15 to 25k a month if possible, and roughly 100M tokens a month is what you estimated? Is that still right, Tom?
[00:40] Tom: Yeah, ballpark. Our agent workloads generate about 200 tokens in, 800 tokens out per call on average. For peak product features it's closer to 1.5k out but most are smaller.
[00:50] Jenna: Cool, that's helpful. So quick taxonomy: Hosted is lowest friction — pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing. Dedicated is reserved capacity — lower unit cost if you commit, predictable throughput and isolation. Private is VPC/on-prem — lowest unit if you absorb infra, but higher ops and upfront.
[01:05] Leo: Ops is big for us; we need SSO, KMS, and audit logs. Also we care about residency for EU customers.
[01:12] Samir: Totally — we support SAML/SSO, KMS integrations, and region pinning for data residency. We'll include the SOC2 pack in the follow-up.
[01:20] Tom: On costs: can you walk through a simple calc? We want line-of-sight to how batching/caching moves the needle.
[01:27] Jenna: Sure. A simple hosted baseline for your shape: assume per-token blended at $0.0006 per token for generation (that's example; we'll send a detailed spreadsheet). At 100M tokens that's about $60k/mo which is above your target.
[01:42] Aisha: Okay that's the rough delta.
[01:45] Jenna: Now three levers to lower that: batching, KV/prefix caching, and a Dedicated commit which reduces unit cost. For your workload: batching (latency tolerant paths) can increase throughput and improve GPU utilization — depending on latency SLOs you might get 10-30% lower cost from batching alone.
[02:02] Tom: What about caching? We have many repeat prompts and a handful of long-lived contexts.
[02:06] Jenna: Prefix or KV cache is huge there — if 30% of tokens are repeat prefixes you can cut those tokens out of generation cost. In practice we've seen 20-60% effective token reduction on customer workloads with good prompt reuse.
[02:18] Samir: To illustrate, if you can cache 30% and batching saves 20% you drop from 100M effective tokens to ~56M effective generation tokens. At $0.0006/token that's roughly $33.6k. Then Dedicated commit discounts can bring per-token further down — often 50-65% off depending on commit and utilization, which could bring you into the 12k-17k/mo range.
[02:45] Leo: So Dedicated math needs utilization to be worth it. What's the commit look like?
[02:49] Jenna: Typical reserved plans start at a monthly commit equivalent we'll lay out in the spreadsheet. If your utilization is high (70%+), Dedicated makes sense. We also offer burst capacity back to hosted for spikes which helps avoid overcommit.
[03:02] Tom: Any hidden fees — storage of KV caches, extra tracing?
[03:07] Samir: Nothing sneaky. Storage/retention is configurable; long-term retention for audit logs or evals is an add-on. We'll call those out.
[03:12] Aisha: You mentioned quantization and model variants — how much cheaper are those?
[03:16] Jenna: Quantized model variants can reduce runtime cost because they use smaller kernels and fit more in GPU memory — that's another 10-40% depending on model and accuracy tradeoff. We recommend running evals to check quality impact.
[03:27] Tom: Ok so putting it together: hosted baseline 60k, with caching+batching down to ~33k, with Dedicated commit potentially down to our target 15-20k if utilization is high and we accept some ops commitment.
[03:41] Samir: Exactly. And Private on-prem could be cheaper at scale but you'd carry infra and ops. For regulated EU-only workloads Private/VPC is common because of residency plus cost if you already run GPUs.
[03:53] Nina: For the pilot, what data do you need from us?
[03:56] Jenna: We need a week of representative traffic: requests per minute over time, average prompt/response lengths, top 50 prompts, and any SLOs (p95 latency targets). Also security checklist answers for SOC2/KMS.
[04:08] Tom: We'll share that. We may obfuscate content but give sizes.
[04:11] Aisha: How long is the pilot and what does it cost?
[04:14] Samir: Pilot typically 2-4 weeks. We can do a cost-neutral pilot where you pay for cloud usage only; or we can cover a small portion depending on scope. Jenna will detail options.
[04:25] Jenna: On benchmarks we'll run your sample traffic through our hosted and dedicated configs so you can see latency and unit cost numbers. We'll also show how caching affects token counts.
[04:34] Tom: Competitors — we've spoken to Replicate and are evaluating self-hosting. How do you compare on cost?
[04:39] Samir: Replicate/Self-host can be cheaper if you optimize heavily and manage infra — but you trade time and reliability. Our differentiator is unified tooling + predictable performance and the route to Dedicated/Private without re-architecting. We'll send side-by-side economics in the spreadsheet.
[04:53] Leo: SLA questions: what uptime and latency guarantees do you offer on Dedicated?
[04:57] Jenna: We have SLA tiers — we'll include targets in the docs. Dedicated gets stronger SLOs and dedicated capacity guarantees; hosted has best-effort with higher redundancy.
[05:06] Nina: On encryption: KMS and HSM support?
[05:09] Samir: Yes, customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM for keys on Private deployments. We'll share the integration guide.
[05:16] Tom: Great. Last Q: any quick wins we should try before committing?
[05:20] Jenna: Start by measuring cacheable prefix rate and implement SVG prompt deduping or client-side caching to reduce tokens sent. Also consider reducing generation temperature if you can — shorter outputs reduce tokens. We'll put a checklist.
[05:33] Samir: Alright let's recap: we send cost model spreadsheet and SOC2/security docs, Jenna schedules pilot and runbook, Ironclad shares traffic profile. We'll target follow-up next week to review pilot scope and pricing.
[05:46] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:49] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up via email with attachments and a calendar invite.
[05:53] (call ends)
